_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Portable pattern-recognition methodology for auditing recurring issues, clustering errors, detecting convention drift,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "I keep seeing the same null-pointer crash in three different files — what's the systemic fix?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the pattern-recognition skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is pattern-recognition the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes pattern-recognition as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against lint-overlay, refactor, naming-conventions
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the pattern-recognition workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore pattern-recognition
Does not route to lint-overlay, refactor, naming-conventions when the pattern-recognition scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
